quote: Prove that the MSG distribution complies with the ordering with the highest likelihood (the likelihood ratio ordering). Assume that X and Y are two independent Random variables with probability distribution function f_x(x; lambda, theta) and f_y(x; beta, alpha). If lambda < alpha and theta < beta, then Lambda = f_x(x;lambda,theta)/f_y(x;beta,alpha) = [theta^2/(lambda+1) (lambda*theta/2 x^2 + (theta+x)/(theta^2+1)) e^{-theta x}] / [alpha^2/(beta+1) (beta*alpha/2 x^2 + (alpha+x)/(alpha^2+1)) e^{-alpha x}]. ... Differentiating with respect to x ... Hence, d log[Lambda]/dx < 0 if lambda < beta, theta < alpha.
family: MGSD (mixture of gamma(3,theta) and Shanker(theta) with mixing proportions lambda^2/(lambda+1)... printed lambda/... and 1/(lambda+1)): f(x;lambda,theta) = theta^2/(lambda+1) (lambda*theta/2 x^2 + (theta+x)/(theta^2+1)) e^{-theta x}, x>0, theta,lambda>0
compared: X ~ MGSD(lambda, theta) vs Y ~ MGSD(beta, alpha)

hypotheses.text: If lambda < alpha and theta < beta

conclusion.direction: X <=_lr Y (density ratio Lambda decreasing in x)
